body.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{hist}}(b,L)\), \(K_\delta(P)=0\), \(V_P>0\), and the corrected posterior satisfies \[d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\!\left(\sqrt n\{\Psi_\delta^*-\mathbb P_nm_P\}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\right),\mathcal N(0,V_P)\right)\to0\] in \(P\)-probability. Its equal-tailed interval has pointwise frequentist coverage \(P\{\Psi_\delta(P)\in C_n^\gamma\}\to1-\gamma\). The class violates strong overlap because \(e(x)=x\) on \([0,1]\), and posterior draws are not constrained to remain on the true side of the cap.
body.justification: The theorem delivers efficient Gaussian posterior uncertainty and nominal coverage for the policy-natural hard cap without restoring overlap.
body.gap: Schmidt and Wikle prove this conclusion for smooth intervention maps; the capped map fails their Taylor and pointwise-Lipschitz steps, which the exact remainder and boundary-bin theorem replace.
body.consumer: An analysis of capped enrollment, prescribing, or encouragement probabilities can report calibrated posterior intervals even when baseline treatment probabilities approach zero or one.
